exam.subject: Citizenship
exam.title: Grade 8 National Examination 2019 – Citizenship

parts.title: Multiple choice
parts.instructions: It has 50 multiple choice questions (1-50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose one best answer and blacken the letter of your choice on the separate answer sheet.

source.document: raw/2019_Citizenship__V-A.pdf (7 pages, text layer; cover '5-CITIZENSHIP, VERSION-A')
source.other_version: raw/2019_Citizenship__V-B.pdf (image-only scan; same 50 questions, V-A reversed in blocks of 10, options shuffled) – used only for cross-checking
source.notes: Transcribed from the V-A text layer and checked against the page images (bold-underlined words such as 'not', 'except', 'wrong' are kept as <u>…</u>). No figures.
source.printing_note: The V-A cover text layer contains a hidden duplicate time line ('1 hour and 40 minutes (100 minutes)'); the visible line is 1 hour and 10 minutes (70 minutes). The V-B cover prints '1 hour and 10 minutes (100 minutes)' (typo). Q24 is printed '24' without the full stop.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: One of the following ethnic groups <u>does not</u> speak a language similar to its name.
explanation_steps: Eritrea has nine ethnic groups. They are grouped by the language they speak (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 37).
The Afar speak Afar, the Tigre speak Tigre and the Bedaweit speak Bedawiet (To-Bedawie).
The Rashaida speak Arabic, not a language called 'Rashaida'. Answer: C.
The Grade 6 textbook asks this same question (p. 44).
questions.explain_simple: The Rashaida people speak Arabic. The other groups speak a language with the same name.
tips: Remember: Rashaida → Arabic.

similar_questions.stem: How are the nine ethnic groups of Eritrea mainly classified?
explanation_steps: The textbook says the main criterion is the language they speak. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The color that represents minerals in the Eritrean national flag is________
explanation_steps: The colours of the flag: green for agriculture (the fertile land), blue for the sea, red for the bloodshed/bravery in the struggle, and yellow for the minerals (textbook: Citizenship Grade 7, p. 92).
So yellow represents minerals. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Yellow in our flag stands for minerals (like gold).
tips: Yellow = minerals (think of gold); blue = sea; green = farming; red = blood of the martyrs.

similar_questions.stem: The blue colour in the Eritrean flag stands for:
explanation_steps: Blue is for the sea. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 7 textbook – Unit 7 – Our National Symbols and Holidays, 7.1 Our national flag – meaning of the colours, p. 92

questions.stem: Our Martyrs Day
explanation_steps: Eritrea remembers its martyrs on 20 June every year (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, p. 103).
September 1 is the start of the armed struggle, May 24 is Independence Day, March 8 is Women's Day. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Martyrs Day is on June 20.
tips: Make a list of the national days and their dates and learn it.

similar_questions.stem: Independence Day in Eritrea is on:
explanation_steps: Eritrea celebrates Independence Day on 24 May. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 7 – Symbols of National Identity, 7.2.2 June 20 Martyrs' Day, p. 103
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Which branch of a government makes the law?
explanation_steps: A government has three branches: legislative, executive and judicial (textbook: Citizenship Grade 7, p. 71).
The legislative branch (in Eritrea, the National Assembly) makes the laws. The executive carries them out; the judicial branch interprets them. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The legislative branch makes laws.
tips: Legislative = law-making; Executive = doing/carrying out; Judicial = judging in courts.

similar_questions.stem: Which branch of government works through the courts?
explanation_steps: Courts belong to the judicial branch. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 7 textbook – Unit 5 – The State of Eritrea, Branches of government, p. 71-72
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: The following are qualities of a good citizen, <u>except</u>:

options.A: One who knows his/her rights and responsibilities
options.C: One who does not pay taxes

explanation_steps: A good citizen knows rights and responsibilities, obeys the law, respects others and pays taxes (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 107).
Not paying taxes is the opposite of a good citizen. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Good citizens pay taxes. So 'does not pay taxes' is not a quality of a good citizen.
tips: In 'except' questions, look for the one bad or different option.

similar_questions.stem: Which one is a quality of a good citizen?
explanation_steps: A good citizen helps the community. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 9 – Being a Good Citizen, 9.1 Qualities of a Good Citizen, p. 107
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: One having immoral values can:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: a person having immoral values tends to develop enemies and engage in crime (Citizenship Grade 8, p. 11).
Good friendship, good choices and respect come from good moral values. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: A person with bad values makes enemies.
tips: Moral = good and right; immoral = bad and wrong.

similar_questions.stem: A person with high moral values:
explanation_steps: Moral values help us tell right from wrong. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 1 – A Disciplined Young Person, 1.3.2 Becoming a person of high moral values, p. 11
textbook_ref.topic: 1.3.2 Becoming a person of high moral values
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: One of the following is a benefit of doing the right thing:
explanation_steps: When you do the right thing you feel calm and happy inside: you have peace of mind (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, Unit 8, p. 110).
Rejection, punishment and loss of confidence are results of doing wrong things. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Doing the right thing gives you peace of mind.
tips: Benefits are good results; the other three are bad results.

similar_questions.stem: What is a result of doing wrong things?
explanation_steps: Doing wrong makes us feel guilty. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A person who is a member of a blood donation group is:
explanation_steps: Giving blood helps sick and injured people. It is a patriotic, voluntary act (textbook: Citizenship Grade 7, pp. 87–88).
So a blood donor is a good and active citizen. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: A blood donor helps others, so he or she is a good and active citizen.
tips: An active citizen does something to help the community.

similar_questions.stem: Which activity shows an active citizen?
explanation_steps: Planting trees helps the community. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is <u>not</u> a respectful behavior?

options.A: I listen attentively when someone is talking to me.
options.B: I say “Please!” whenever I ask someone for help.
options.C: I make fun of people when they do things that I don’t like.
options.D: I say, “thank you!” whenever someone helps me.

explanation_steps: Listening, saying 'please' and saying 'thank you' are all ways to show respect (textbook: Citizenship Grade 7, Unit 1).
Making fun of people hurts them. It is not respectful. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Laughing at people is not respect.
tips: Respect means treating others the way you want to be treated.

similar_questions.stem: Which one shows respect?
explanation_steps: Saying 'thank you' is respectful. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 7 textbook – Unit 1 – Being Respectful, Being Respectful, p. 1
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Who can be a good model from the following persons?

options.A: A person who doesn’t respect the law.
options.B: A trader who doesn’t pay taxes.
options.C: A soldier who fulfills his/her duty
options.D: A young person who do not participate in communal activities.

explanation_steps: A good model (role model) is a person whose good actions we copy.
A soldier who does his or her duty serves the country. The others break the law, avoid taxes or do not help the community. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A soldier who does his or her duty is a good example for others.
tips: A role model does good things that others can copy.

similar_questions.stem: Which person is a good role model?

options.B: A doctor who helps the poor for free
options.C: A driver who breaks traffic rules
options.D: A worker who is always late

explanation_steps: Helping the poor is a good example. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 6 – We are Patriots, 6.1 Patriotic role models, p. 90
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: In the referendum ___________ of the voters said, “Yes” for independence.
explanation_steps: In the referendum of April 1993, 99.8% of the voters said 'YES' to independence (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 64).
Answer: B. (The same question is in the Grade 6 textbook review, p. 74.)
questions.explain_simple: 99.8% of the voters said 'Yes'.
tips: Referendum 1993: 99.8% 'Yes'.

similar_questions.stem: In which year was the Eritrean referendum held?
explanation_steps: The referendum was held in April 1993. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 5 – The State of Eritrea, The referendum, p. 64
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: When people do what they are supposed to do, it is called ___________
explanation_steps: A responsibility is a duty, something someone should do (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 103).
A right is something we are allowed to have or do. So the answer is responsibility. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Doing what you should do is your responsibility.
tips: Right = what you may have; responsibility = what you must do.

similar_questions.stem: Going to school and getting an education is a child's:
explanation_steps: Education is a right of every child. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 8 – Rules, Rights and Responsibilities, Rules, rights and responsibilities, p. 103
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Which one is <u>not</u> part of the Executive Branch?
explanation_steps: The Executive Branch consists of the president, the ministers and the commissioners (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 71).
The (National) Assembly is the legislative branch. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The Assembly makes laws. It is not part of the executive.
tips: Executive = President + ministers + commissioners.

similar_questions.stem: The National Assembly belongs to the:
explanation_steps: The Assembly makes laws: legislative. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 5 – The State of Eritrea, Branches of government, p. 71
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: The following are earlier works of literature in Eritrea, except:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: the earlier works of literature included translations and collections of folklores, traditional poems, fables and proverbs (Citizenship Grade 8, p. 41).
Textbooks are not in this list. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Folklores, proverbs and fables are old literature. Textbooks are not.
tips: Early Eritrean literature came from oral traditions: stories, poems, fables and proverbs.

similar_questions.stem: A short wise saying passed from old people to young people is a:
explanation_steps: That is a proverb. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 3 – Knowing our Culture and Society, 3.4 Eritrean Literature, p. 41
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Knowing our Culture and Society

questions.stem: One of the following revolutions was against slavery:
explanation_steps: The textbook says the Haitian Revolution of 1791 was against slavery. It was led by the slaves against the French colonialists (Citizenship Grade 8, p. 49).
The Algerian revolution was against French colonial rule; the French revolution was against the king. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The slaves of Haiti fought against slavery.
tips: Haiti → slavery; Algeria → French colonialism; France → the king.

similar_questions.stem: Haiti became independent in:
explanation_steps: Haiti became independent in 1804. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 4 – The Eritrean Revolution, 4.2 Revolutions around the World, p. 49
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Which one is different from the others?
explanation_steps: The Grade 6 textbook (p. 47) says: some countries revolted against their own governments, for example the Russian, the French and the Chinese revolutions.
Other revolutions, like the Eritrean, Algerian and Vietnamese revolutions, were against colonial governments.
So the Vietnamese revolution is the different one. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Russia, France and China fought their own governments. Vietnam fought a colonial government.
tips: Group revolutions into two kinds: against their own government, or against colonisers.

similar_questions.stem: Which revolution was against a colonial government?
explanation_steps: Algeria fought French colonial rule. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 4 – The Eritrean Revolution, Revolutions (against own governments / against colonial governments), p. 47
textbook_ref.topic: Revolutions (against own governments / against colonial governments)
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.section: Revolutions (against own governments / against colonial governments)

questions.review_flag: The question gives no criterion. Keyed D from the textbook grouping (G6 p.47: Russian, French, Chinese = against their own governments; Vietnamese = against colonial rule). A student could also argue C (the French Revolution is the only 18th-century, non-communist one).

questions.stem: One is <u>wrong</u> about the Eritrean liberation struggle period:

options.A: Roads, hospitals, schools, houses, factories and farmlands were destroyed.
options.B: Eritreans were forced to leave their country and live as refugees.
options.C: The Eritrean people had everything they needed to work, learn and prosper.
options.D: Tens of thousands of defenseless children, women and men were killed.

explanation_steps: During the 30-year struggle there was great destruction: people were killed, property was destroyed and many became refugees (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 61).
So it is wrong to say the people had everything they needed to prosper. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: During the war, life was very hard. People did not have everything they needed.
tips: Look for the option that does not fit a time of war.

similar_questions.stem: During the liberation struggle many Eritreans had to live in other countries as:
explanation_steps: They were refugees. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 4 – The Eritrean Revolution, The Eritrean Revolution – the price of freedom, p. 61
textbook_ref.topic: The Eritrean Revolution – the price of freedom
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.section: The Eritrean Revolution – the price of freedom

questions.stem: One of the following is <u>not</u> true about the Eritrean Revolution:

options.A: It was a revolution which was conducted to change the government.

explanation_steps: The textbook groups the Eritrean Revolution with revolutions against colonial governments: Eritreans fought to get their independence, not only to change a government (Citizenship Grade 6, p. 47).
It was popular (the people took part), just, and resilient (it won after many challenges – Citizenship Grade 8, p. 51). Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The Eritrean Revolution was for independence from colonisers, not just to change a government.
tips: The Eritrean Revolution: popular, just, resilient, for independence.

similar_questions.stem: The Eritrean armed struggle is called resilient because:

options.B: it won after overcoming many challenges

explanation_steps: It came to victory after overcoming numerous challenges. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 4 – The Eritrean Revolution, 4.3 The Eritrean Revolution – resilience, p. 51
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Referendum was conducted:

options.A: because the Europeans forced Eritrea to do so.
options.B: to show the world the downfall of the Dergue.
options.C: because there was a doubt that the Eritrean people might vote against independence.
options.D: to make our independence legal and get international recognition

explanation_steps: After liberation in 1991, a referendum was held in April 1993 so that independence would be legal and recognised by the world (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, pp. 64–65; Grade 8, p. 67).
There was no doubt about the people's choice (99.8% said 'Yes'). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The referendum made independence legal and brought world recognition.
tips: Referendum → legal independence → international recognition.

similar_questions.stem: The referendum of 1993 was supervised to show that the vote was:
explanation_steps: The vote was free and fair. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 5 – The State of Eritrea, The referendum, p. 64-65
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Eritrea has officially declared its independence on:
explanation_steps: Eritrea was liberated on 24 May 1991, but it officially declared its independence on 24 May 1993, after the referendum (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, p. 70).
Answer: D. (Sept. 1, 1961 is the start of the armed struggle.)
questions.explain_simple: Independence was officially declared on 24 May 1993, after the referendum.
tips: 1991 = liberation; 1993 = referendum and official independence.

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea was liberated from Ethiopian rule on:
explanation_steps: Liberation day was 24 May 1991. Answer: A.

questions.stem: ______________ has been declared a national holiday for the purpose of honoring and showing respect to all those who died struggling for the nation’s freedom.
explanation_steps: People who died for the nation's freedom are called martyrs. Martyrs Day (20 June) has been declared a national holiday to honour them (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, p. 106).
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Martyrs Day honours the people who died for our freedom.
tips: Martyr = a person who died for the country.

similar_questions.stem: On which date is Martyrs Day?
explanation_steps: June 20. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 7 – Symbols of National Identity, 7.2.2 Martyrs' Day, p. 103-106
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: The voting of people during an election of people’s representative for the National Assembly is:
explanation_steps: Rights about taking part in government – voting, being elected – are political rights (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, p. 73).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Voting in an election is a political right.
tips: Politics is about government, so voting is political.

similar_questions.stem: The right to own property and work is mainly an:
explanation_steps: Work and property are economic. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 5 – The Birth of the Free State of Eritrea, Democracy – political rights, p. 73
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 5 – The Birth of the Free State of Eritrea

questions.stem: One of the following is <u>not</u> the means of expressing our patriotism.

options.C: Reading books about our armed struggle.

explanation_steps: Patriotism is love of your country (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 80).
Singing patriotic songs, joining community work and learning our history show this love. Destroying public property harms the country. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: A patriot protects public property. Destroying it is not patriotism.
tips: Patriotism = love of the country, shown by actions that help it.

similar_questions.stem: Which action shows patriotism?
explanation_steps: Planting trees helps the country. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 6 – Becoming a Young Eritrean Patriot, Patriotism, p. 80
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Becoming a Young Eritrean Patriot

questions.stem: The following are some ways of respecting our national flag, <u>except</u>:

options.A: The flag should usually be hoisted from sunrise to sunset.
options.B: The flag should never touch the ground.
options.C: Anyone who wears a hat should remove it during flag ceremony.
options.D: The flag should be waved upside down.

explanation_steps: The textbook rules include: hoist the flag from sunrise to sunset; it should never touch the ground; it should never be waved upside down (Citizenship Grade 8, pp. 98–99).
So waving it upside down is not respectful. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The flag must never be upside down.
tips: Learn the flag rules: sunrise to sunset, never on the ground, never upside down.

similar_questions.stem: During the flag ceremony, students should:

options.B: stand still and sing the national anthem

explanation_steps: Students stand still and sing the anthem. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 7 – Symbols of National Identity, Respecting our national flag, p. 98-99
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: The statement “All boys hate to cook” expresses
explanation_steps: A stereotype is an oversimplified statement about all members of a group (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, p. 37).
'All boys hate to cook' says the same thing about every boy. That is a stereotype. Answer: A.
Prejudice is to pre-judge or form an opinion before knowing a person; etiquette means good manners.
questions.explain_simple: Saying 'all boys' are the same is a stereotype.
tips: Words like 'all' or 'every' about a group often show a stereotype.

similar_questions.stem: 'All girls are bad at football' is an example of:
explanation_steps: It is an oversimplified statement about all girls. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 3 – Knowing our Culture and Society, Stereotype and prejudice, p. 37
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Knowing our Culture and Society

questions.stem: The following are the possible consequences of wrongful acts, <u>except</u>:
explanation_steps: Wrong acts bring bad results: losing opportunities, prison and feeling guilty (textbook: Citizenship Grade 8, Unit 8).
Promotion (moving up to a better job or class) is a reward for good work, not a result of wrongdoing. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Promotion is a reward. It does not come from doing wrong.
tips: Consequences of wrong acts are always bad.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a possible consequence of stealing?
explanation_steps: Stealing can lead to prison. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 8 – Our Acts and their Consequences: Right and Wrong, 8.1 Doing the Right Thing – consequences, p. 110-111
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 8 – Our Acts and their Consequences: Right and Wrong

questions.stem: Who is not considered a hero/heroine from the following?

options.A: A person who sacrifices his/her life for the benefit of the people.
options.B: An athlete who wins representing his/her country on international competitions
options.C: A person who collaborates with an enemy
options.D: A person who works and helps his/her community with his/her expertise.

explanation_steps: A hero or heroine does brave or great things for the people and the country (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, p. 50).
A person who works with the enemy betrays the people. He or she is not a hero. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Helping the enemy is betrayal, not heroism.
tips: Heroes work FOR their people; collaborators work WITH the enemy.

similar_questions.stem: Which person is a hero?

options.A: A fighter who died for independence

explanation_steps: A fighter who died for the people is a hero. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 6 textbook – Unit 4 – The Eritrean Revolution, 4.2 Honoring our Heroes, p. 50
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Identify the statement which <u>does not</u> promote religious harmony.

options.A: A boy tells his girl-friend that his religion is better than hers.
options.B: People of all religions take part in peace march after a riot.
options.C: A girl asked her friend to tell her about religious feasts in her village.
options.D: Schools teach about the basic values that are common to all religions.

explanation_steps: Religious harmony means people of different religions live together peacefully (textbook: Citizenship Grade 7, p. 41 lists these same examples).
Saying 'my religion is better than yours' can cause conflict. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Saying your religion is better than someone else's does not help peace.
tips: Harmony comes from learning about and respecting other religions.

similar_questions.stem: Which action helps religious harmony?

options.B: Visiting a friend on his religious holiday
options.D: Saying only one religion is good

explanation_steps: Visiting a friend on his holiday shows respect. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 7 textbook – Unit 3 – Knowing about our Culture and Society, Religious harmony, p. 41
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Knowing about our Culture and Society

questions.stem: Which of the following is not <u>true</u> about self-control?

options.A: Self-control is the ability to control our emotions, words, actions and desires.
options.B: Self-control is to react forcefully when someone do not agree with your idea.
options.C: Self-control is to show determination and commitment to achieve our goals.
options.D: Self control is what you do when no one is watching.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Self-control is the ability to control our emotions, words, actions and desires' (Citizenship Grade 8, p. 1).
Reacting forcefully (angrily) when someone disagrees shows a LACK of self-control. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Getting angry and forceful is not self-control.
tips: Self-control = stop, think, then act calmly.

similar_questions.stem: Which shows self-control?

options.B: Counting to ten before answering when angry

explanation_steps: Calming down before answering is self-control. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Citizenship Education Grade 8 textbook – Unit 1 – A Disciplined Young Person, 1.1 Self-control, p. 1
textbook_ref.subject: Citizenship Education

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is a quality of a good student?

options.A: As long as I score good marks in the exam, I don’t care what others say about me.
options.B: School is only for gifted students, so I better not waste my time attending classes.
options.C: To look after school properties is the job of the school guards and teachers, so I don’t care if they are destroyed.
options.D: Our semester exam is approaching, so I must reduce my playing time and concentrate on my studies.

explanation_steps: Good students plan their time and study hard, care about others and about school property (textbook: Citizenship Grade 6, pp. 19–30).
Reducing playing time to study before an exam is good time management. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: A good student studies more when the exam is near.
tips: Good students manage their time and care for school property.

similar_questions.stem: A good student:
